f.title: Protocol must specify safety parameters, AE recording/reporting procedures and AESI list
f.statement: The protocol's safety assessment section must specify the safety parameters; the methods and timing for assessing, recording and analysing them; procedures for eliciting, recording and reporting adverse events and intercurrent illnesses; a list of adverse events of special interest and/or expected adverse events (with relatedness to the intervention, rationale, expected rate and laboratory limits); the type and duration of follow-up after adverse events; and provision for dealing with all adverse events, with a copy of the AE report form.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines, food supplements, vaccines and medical devices authorised by FDA Ghana (FDA/CTD/GDL-ACT/2024/05)

rows.quote: 8. Assessment of Safety i. Specification of safety parameters. ii. The methods and timing for assessing, recording, and analyzing safety parameters. iii. Procedures for eliciting reports of and for recording and reporting adverse event and intercurrent illnesses. iv. List of adverse events of special interest (AESI) and/or expected adverse events – information shall include; a. Whether the event is related to the intervention or not. b. Rationale for listing each event c. Expected rate or frequency of each event d. Laboratory limits (if applicable) v. The type and duration of the follow-up of participants after adverse events. vi. Provision for dealing with all adverse events. Copy of form to be used to report adverse event.

f.title: Keep trial data for 5 years (20 years for NDA) after completion and make available to FDA
f.statement: All clinical and experimental data (electronic or paper) shall be kept in a secured place for 5 years after completion of the trial, and 20 years for a New Drug Application, and be made readily available for review on request by the Authority. The protocol should describe the procedure for keeping the participant list and detailed CRF records for each participant.

f.title: Notify substantial amendments likely to affect participant safety

f.title: Assess whether safety report data require a substantial amendment
f.statement: A safety report is not itself an amendment, but the sponsor has to verify whether the data it presents require a change to the documentation submitted with the clinical trial application; if that change is substantial, the rules for notification of substantial amendments apply.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines, food supplements, vaccines and medical devices authorised by FDA Ghana (FDA/CTD/GDL-ACT/2024/05)

rows.quote: Safety report (SR) is not per se an amendment and thus does not have to be notified as a substantial amendment to The Authority. However, the sponsor has to verify whether the data presented in the SR requires a change to the documentation submitted with the request for authorization of a clinical trial. If this amendment is substantial, the rules for notification of substantial amendments apply to these changes.
